The assembly apparatus includes a work base, a first robot, a second robot, and a controller that coordinates the operation of these components.

The work base is provided with a placement surface on which multiple works are individually placed. The placement surface is configured to circulate the works through a plurality of work areas arranged along a circumference. The works are moved from one work area to another at fixed time intervals, so that each work sequentially reaches different processing positions around the circumference.

The first robot is disposed inside the circumference along which the work areas are arranged. From this inner position, the first robot is capable of accessing multiple work areas on the placement surface. The first robot performs a predetermined process on selected work areas as the works are circulated by the work base.

The second robot is disposed outside the circumference. The second robot is configured to access at least one of the work areas arranged along the circumference. In particular, the second robot assists the process performed by the first robot at one of the work areas.

The controller controls the operation of both the first robot and the second robot. The controller directs the first robot to perform the predetermined process on selected work areas among the plurality of work areas. The controller also directs the second robot to assist the first robot in performing that process at one of the selected work areas. Through this coordinated control, the assembly apparatus can efficiently carry out processing operations on multiple works as they circulate through the work areas.
outputs.L4:
An assembly apparatus includes a work base configured to circulate along a predetermined circulation path. The work base is provided with a plurality of work areas, and each work area is capable of holding a workpiece, component, jig, pallet, or other object to be assembled or processed. As the work base circulates, the respective work areas are successively moved through positions at which assembly operations can be performed.

A first robot is arranged on an inner side of the circulating work base. The first robot is positioned and configured so that its operating range extends to all of the plurality of work areas provided on the work base. Accordingly, the first robot can perform predetermined assembly processes, handling processes, inspection processes, fastening processes, or other required operations on any selected work area as the work base circulates.

A second robot is arranged on an outer side of the circulating work base. The second robot is configured so that its operating range reaches at least one of the plurality of work areas. The second robot may perform an assisting operation at that work area, such as supplying a component, holding a part, supporting an assembly step, tightening or bonding a member, removing a completed product, or carrying out an inspection or adjustment. By being disposed outside the circulating work base, the second robot can cooperate with the first robot without interfering with the first robot’s access to the work areas from the inner side.

The assembly apparatus further includes a controller that controls operation of the circulating work base, the first robot, and the second robot. The controller coordinates the timing of movement of the work base and the timing of operations performed by the robots. In particular, during each circulation interval of the work base, the controller causes the first robot to execute predetermined processes on selected ones of the plurality of work areas. At the same time, or in a coordinated sequence, the controller causes the second robot to assist the first robot at one of the selected work areas within the operating range of the second robot.

Through this arrangement, assembly operations can be distributed between the inner first robot and the outer second robot. The first robot can perform operations over the entire set of work areas, while the second robot supplements the operation at a particular work area or group of work areas. Because the controller coordinates the robots according to the circulation timing of the work base, multiple operations can be performed efficiently within a single circulation interval. This reduces idle time, improves synchronization between process steps, and increases the overall efficiency and throughput of the assembly apparatus.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language, yet it often goes unnoticed. It is a small word, but it plays an important role in giving meaning and clarity to sentences. As a definite article, “the” points to something specific. For example, “a book” could mean any book, but “the book” refers to a particular one that the speaker and listener both understand.

The word “the” helps create focus. It can turn a general idea into something exact, familiar, or important. We say “the sun,” “the world,” and “the truth” because these ideas feel unique or well-known. Without “the,” English would sound less clear and less natural.

Although it is simple, “the” is essential. It connects ideas, identifies objects, and helps readers understand what is being discussed. In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an embodiment of an automated assembly apparatus where parts are placed on a circular indexing table, a central robot performs predetermined processes at several stations, and an external robot assists at one of those stations under controller control.
counterfactuals.output:
An embodiment of the automated assembly apparatus includes a circular indexing table on which a plurality of workpieces or parts are positioned at predetermined locations. The indexing table is configured to rotate intermittently, indexing the parts successively through a plurality of circumferentially arranged processing stations.

A central robot is disposed near the center of the circular indexing table. The central robot is controlled to execute predetermined assembly or processing operations on the parts as they arrive at the respective stations. For example, the central robot may perform operations such as positioning, fastening, welding, inspection, dispensing, or component insertion at several of the stations around the indexing table. Because the robot is centrally located, it can access multiple stations without requiring separate robots at each station.

At least one external robot is arranged outside the perimeter of the circular indexing table adjacent to one of the processing stations. The external robot assists the central robot or performs an additional operation at that station, such as supplying a component, holding a part, applying force, removing a completed assembly, or carrying out a specialized process that is more conveniently performed from outside the table.

A controller is operatively connected to the indexing table, the central robot, and the external robot. The controller coordinates rotation of the indexing table with the operation of both robots. In operation, the controller stops the indexing table at an indexed position, causes the central robot to perform one or more predetermined processes at selected stations, and causes the external robot to assist at its assigned station in timed relation with the central robot. After the required operations are completed, the controller indexes the table to move the parts to the next stations and repeats the sequence.

In this arrangement, multiple assembly processes can be carried out in parallel or in a coordinated sequence on parts arranged around the circular table, while the central robot provides flexible multi-station processing and the external robot supplements the operation at a station requiring additional access, tooling, or handling capability.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a formal patent specification summary for a robotic assembly apparatus comprising a circulating work base, multiple circumferential work areas, a first robot accessible to all stations from inside, a second robot accessible from outside to assist, and a controller coordinating operations every cycle.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent Specification Summary

A robotic assembly apparatus is provided for performing sequential or coordinated assembly operations on a workpiece. The apparatus includes a circulating work base configured to move along a predetermined circulating path and to support one or more workpieces during assembly. A plurality of work areas or work stations are arranged circumferentially along the circulating path of the work base, each work area being configured to perform or receive a respective assembly operation during each operational cycle.

A first robot is disposed on an inner side of the circulating work base. The first robot is positioned and configured so that its operating range extends to each of the plurality of circumferential work areas, thereby enabling the first robot to access and perform operations at all work stations from the inside of the circulating path. A second robot is disposed on an outer side of the circulating work base. The second robot is configured to access at least one of the plurality of work areas from outside the circulating path and to assist in assembly operations performed at the corresponding work area, including supplying components, supporting parts, fastening, inspection, or cooperative manipulation with the first robot.

A controller is operatively connected to the circulating work base, the first robot, and the second robot. The controller is configured to coordinate movement of the circulating work base and the operations of the first and second robots in accordance with a predetermined cycle. During each cycle, the controller indexes or circulates the work base to position workpieces at the plurality of circumferential work areas and controls the first robot to perform operations at one or more of the work areas. The controller further controls the second robot to perform assisting operations from the outside of the circulating work base in timed coordination with the first robot and the movement of the work base.

By arranging the first robot within the circulating work base so as to access all circumferential work areas and arranging the second robot outside the circulating work base for auxiliary or cooperative operation, the apparatus enables compact, efficient, and flexible robotic assembly. The configuration reduces the number of required robots, improves utilization of robotic motion ranges, and permits coordinated assembly operations to be carried out at multiple stations during repeated production cycles.
